title: S2d2 cache-aware tool and skill disclosure in shadow: stable Level-0 tool catalog view and stable skill catalog block, measured on the existing tool_disclosure and skill_selection rows (P9, P10)
spec:
orchestrator/tool_catalog.py exposes a pure function cache_view(role, keep, previous_row) returning {stable_catalog_chars (the Level-0 catalog: names and one-line purposes of every known tool for the role, identical across tasks), dynamic_chars (the selected Level-2 schemas), changed_since_previous (True, False, or None when previous_row is None)}; orchestrator/bus.py (scope), where tool_disclosure rows are written (near line 285), calls it and stores the three fields on the row; previous_row is the last tool_disclosure row of the same role among the most recent 200 decision_log rows (bounded read, no module state). Active presentation ([tool_disclosure].cache_mode active): the stable catalog text precedes the dynamic schemas in the tool disclosure text built for the packet. Skills: orchestrator/skill_router.py exposes catalog_block(role, registry) (sorted ids and triggers of every active skill for the role, identical across tasks); orchestrator/spawn.py (scope), where _prepare_skills builds the presented skills section, prepends that block ONLY when [skills].cache_mode is active, and always records catalog_chars and selected_chars on the existing skill_selection row. Both sections get cache_mode = "shadow" with dated comments and revert instructions, missing key means off, validated in pool (S2d1 adds the validation helper; reuse it), inert when the section's mode is off. Docs: sections 2 and 3 of docs/hermes-hardening/10-cache-aware-disclosure.md with a reproducible command (`orchestrator scorecard --economy --disclosure-cache`, scope orchestrator/cli.py) printing row counts, date range, mean stable vs dynamic chars and the share of runs whose dynamic list changed since the previous task of the role; when no rows exist the doc says so.
Spec review T-1293 folded in: (1) One helper, two callers: tool_catalog.cache_view(role, kept_ids, previous_row) is pure; the two existing tool_disclosure row writers call it: spawn._shadow_tool_disclosure (Claude roles) and bus.log_run's Codex row; the escalation row (reason hidden_tool_requested) is left untouched and never used as a previous row. (2) previous_row = the most recent tool_disclosure row for the same role whose subject is a DIFFERENT task and which carries deterministic.kept; found through a new bounded helper decision_log.last_row(kind, *, role, exclude_subject, require_key) that reads only today's decision_log file from the end (scope adds orchestrator/decision_log.py and tests/test_decision_log.py); an older row without the new fields still qualifies as previous when it has kept; none found -> changed_since_previous None. (3) changed_since_previous compares the SETS of kept ids (order ignored). (4) Level-0 catalog = tool_catalog.level0(ids) rendered as one line per tool (name and purpose) over the role's static disclosed id list (no mcp measurements, so it is identical across tasks); Level-2 = the schema text tool_catalog.disclosed(role) already renders; the active ordering is applied in the spawn.py function that renders disclosed tools into the prompt (find it as the caller of tool_catalog.disclosed and name it in the docs), with an acceptance test asserting the stable block precedes the schemas only in active mode. (5) Skills: catalog_block is prepended inside spawn._prepare_skills as before; both cache_mode keys validated by the S2d1 helper pattern (a small cache_mode(cfg, section) in tool_catalog/skill_router, invalid -> off with invalid_config on the row).
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_tool_catalog.py::test_cache_view_stable_across_tasks_and_changed_flag_none_first (identical stable text for two tasks of a role; changed flag None without a previous row, True/False with one)

spec_review_risks.issue: last_row filters by role, but decision_log.record only sets a top-level role when the caller passes role=. Neither tool_disclosure writer (spawn.py:484, bus.py:290) passes it. The role sits in deterministic.role, so a filter on row['role'] matches nothing and previous_row is always None. The spec must say to match deterministic.role, or to make both writers pass role=.

last_row reads only today's decision_log file. After midnight (Europe/Zurich, or UTC, depending on schedlog) or on the first task of the day, changed_since_previous is None even when a previous row exists yesterday. The scorecard share then depends on when the run happened, and this is a silent fallback. The spec should either read yesterday's file as well (still bounded) or state the limitation in the docs and count None rows separately.

log_run writes a Codex tool_disclosure row on every codex event or attempt for a task, not once per task. Rows are duplicated per task, which skews the row counts, the mean stable and dynamic chars and the changed share in the scorecard. The spec should require one row per task or dedupe by subject in the scorecard. The Codex row also has candidates=['CODEX_TOOLS'] and no static disclosed id list. tool_catalog.disclosed('codex_execute') is unverified, so the spec should say what the Level-0 catalog is for codex_execute (stable_catalog_chars may be 0). The write sits inside a bare try/except that swallows errors, so a cache_view failure silently drops the whole existing row. Compute cache_view in its own guard so the existing row still gets written.

The spec says 'find it as the caller of tool_catalog.disclosed'. The real callers at spawn.py:469 and :1493 only build row candidates and do not render prompt text. It does not say which function builds the tool disclosure text for the packet, or whether one exists. It should name the function, or require the implementer to create it. The active-order acceptance test cannot be written without that. The second caller (spawn.py:1492, escalation row) must stay untouched.

cache_mode(cfg, section) is added in both tool_catalog and skill_router, and the spec cites 'the S2d1 helper' as context_router.cache_mode. That helper raises ValueError, and spawn._context_mode wraps it to set invalid_config. The spec should say to reuse one shared helper, or how the two copies differ, so it does not create three divergent validators. It should also say that invalid config records invalid_config on the skill_selection and tool_disclosure rows, and that cache_mode is inert when the section's mode is off (tool_disclosure mode from promotion.mode, skill_routing mode).

The [tool_disclosure] and [skills] sections need a cache_mode key with a dated comment. Line 358 already has one for context_router, and a test_pool.py check for unknown keys or values may need updating. That test file is not in scope. Verify that adding the keys does not break it, or add tests/test_pool.py to scope.

The scorecard spec does not define how rows with changed_since_previous None are counted. It should say the denominator for 'share of runs whose dynamic list changed' excludes None rows and that the None count is printed. It should also specify the date range source (row ts, ISO dates, Europe/Zurich), the zero-row output text, and whether Codex and Claude rows are pooled or split by role. The acceptance test should assert exact fields.

decision_log._bounded may truncate large rows. If it trims deterministic.kept, or the new char fields, then last_row's require_key check and the set comparison in changed_since_previous become unreliable. The spec should confirm the kept list survives _bounded, or add a test.
